    44	\section{Key theorem forms}
    45	
    46	Three statements must be kept apart.  Throughout, $\game$ denotes a symmetric
    47	two-player one-round game and $\eps \ge 0$ a real parameter; the notation is
    48	introduced in the next section.
    49	
    50	\begin{enumerate}
    51	  \item \textbf{Source form (attainment form).}  If
    52	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and projective
    53	  strategy $\strategy$ with $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps$.
    54	  \item \textbf{Approximate form (what the source proof establishes).}  If
    55	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then for every $\eps' > \eps$ there exists a
    56	  symmetric and projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    57	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps'$.
    58	  \item \textbf{Given-strategy form (value-preserving symmetrization).}  If
    59	  $\strategy'$ is any strategy for $\game$ with
    60	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and
    61	  projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    62	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) = \val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$.
    63	\end{enumerate}
    64	
    65	The source proof consists exactly of a proof of the third form, applied to a
    66	strategy supplied by the definition of the supremum; this yields the second
    67	form.  The first form asserts strictly more than the second, and the passage
    68	from the second to the first is the gap discussed in this note.  Every use of
    69	the lemma, in the source and in this project, consumes only the second or the
    70	third form.
    71	
    72	\section{The source assertion}
    73	
    74	A two-player one-round game
    75	$\game = (\mathcal X, \mathcal A, \mu, D)$ in compact symmetric notation
    76	consists of a finite question alphabet $\mathcal X$, a finite answer alphabet
    77	$\mathcal A$, a symmetric question distribution $\mu$ on
    78	$\mathcal X \times \mathcal X$, and a decision predicate $D$ treating the two
    79	players symmetrically.  A tensor product strategy
    80	$\strategy = (\ket\psi, A, B)$ consists of a unit vector $\ket\psi$ in a
    81	tensor product $\mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ of \emph{finite-dimensional}
    82	Hilbert spaces together with POVMs $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ for the two
    83	players; its value $\val^*(\game, \strategy)$ is the acceptance probability,
    84	and the value of the game is the supremum
    85	\begin{equation*}
    86	  \val^*(\game) = \sup_{\strategy} \val^*(\game, \strategy)
    87	\end{equation*}
    88	over all tensor product strategies.  A strategy is projective if all its
    89	measurements are projective, and symmetric if the state is
    90	permutation-invariant on $\mathcal H \ot \mathcal H$ and both players use the
    91	same measurements.
    92	
    93	The symmetrization lemma of \cite[Section~5]{Ji2020MIPStar} asserts:%
    94	\footnote{The statement is at
    95	\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~94--99,
    96	and its proof at lines~101--132.  The blueprint statement restored to this form
    97	is \path{lem:symmetric-strat} in
    98	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}.}
    99	if $\game$ is a symmetric game with $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some
   100	$\eps \ge 0$, then
   101	\begin{equation*}
   102	  \exists\, \strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M) \text{ symmetric and projective}
   103	  \quad\text{with}\quad
   104	  \val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps.
   105	  \tag{\path{lem:symmetric-strat}}
   106	\end{equation*}
   107	
   108	Its proof runs as follows.  For every $\eps' > \eps$ the definition of the
   109	supremum supplies a strategy $\strategy' = (\ket{\psi'}, A, B)$ with
   110	$\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps'$.  By Naimark dilation in the completed
   111	projective form of \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} one may take
   112	$\ket{\psi'} \in \C^d_{A'} \ot \C^d_{B'}$ for some integer $d$ with all
   113	measurements projective.  One then forms the permutation-invariant state
   114	\begin{equation*}
   115	  \ket{\psi} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}
   116	  \bigl( \ket{0}_A \ket{1}_B \ket{\psi'}_{A'B'}
   117	       + \ket{1}_A \ket{0}_B \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{A'B'} \bigr)
   118	\end{equation*}
   119	on $(\C^2 \ot \C^d) \ot (\C^2 \ot \C^d)$, where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ permutes
   120	the two players' registers, and the block-diagonal projective measurements
   121	$M^x_a = \ket{0}\!\bra{0} \ot A^x_a + \ket{1}\!\bra{1} \ot B^x_a$.  Symmetry
   122	of $D$ gives $\val^*(\game, (\ket\psi, M)) = \val^*(\game, \strategy')$.  The
   123	construction is therefore \emph{value-preserving}: applied to any strategy it
   124	produces a symmetric projective strategy of exactly the same value.  What the
   125	proof establishes is thus the given-strategy form, hence the approximate form;
   126	the printed conclusion is the attainment form.
   127	
   128	\section{Why attainment does not follow}
   129	
   130	The supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ ranges over strategies on
   131	finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces of unbounded dimension.  The strategies
   132	$\strategy'_{\eps'}$ produced for $\eps' \downarrow \eps$ may require
   133	dimensions $d(\eps')$ growing without bound, and there is no compactness
   134	across dimensions from which a limiting finite-dimensional strategy of value
   135	at least $1-\eps$ could be extracted.  A symmetric projective strategy of
   136	value at least $1-\eps = \val^*(\game)$ would attain the supremum, so the
   137	printed conclusion is equivalent, under its hypothesis, to the assertion that
   138	$\val^*(\game)$ is attained by some strategy.  No general principle supplies
   139	this: it is known, and recalled in the introduction of the source itself, that
   140	the set of finite-dimensional quantum correlations is not closed and differs
   141	from the set of infinite-dimensional spatial correlations, so limits of
   142	finite-dimensional strategies need not be realized by any finite-dimensional
   143	strategy.  Whether some symmetric game realizes the failure --- a game whose
   144	value is attained by no tensor product strategy, presented together with the
   145	exposing functional as a decision predicate --- is a separate question that
   146	this note does not need to settle.  The local verdict is about the proof: the
   147	cited argument proves the approximate form and does not prove the attainment
   148	form.
   149	
   150	\section{Uses of the lemma}
   151	
   152	The source invokes the lemma twice.
   153	
   154	First, in the soundness proof for the oracularization transformation, the
   155	argument fixes a strategy $\strategy^{\mathrm{orac}}$ for the oracularized game
   156	``with value $1-\eps$'' and applies the lemma to assume without loss of
   157	generality that it is projective.%
   158	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/10_oracularization.tex},
   159	lines~317--321.}
   160	Here the input is a given strategy, not the value of the game; the
   161	given-strategy form applies verbatim and preserves the value exactly, so the
   162	use is justified by what the proof establishes.
   163	
   164	Second, in the soundness proof for answer reduction, the argument assumes the
   165	strict inequality $\val^*(\game) > 1-\eps$ and concludes that there is a
   166	symmetric projective strategy of value greater than $1-\eps$.%
   167	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/11_answer_reduction.tex},
   168	lines~2322--2332.}
   169	Writing $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps_0$ with $\eps_0 < \eps$ and applying the
   170	approximate form with $\eps' = (\eps+\eps_0)/2$ produces a symmetric
   171	projective strategy of value at least $1-\eps' > 1-\eps$.  A strict lower
   172	bound on the supremum thus passes through the approximate form; attainment is
   173	not used.
   174	
   175	In this project, the soundness statements of the Pauli basis test track
   176	quantify over strategies assumed to succeed with probability at least
   177	$1-\eps$, so any symmetrization step starts from a given strategy and consumes
   178	the given-strategy form.  The blueprint currently records the lemma as part of
   179	the games vocabulary and has no downstream dependency on it; the two source
   180	uses above belong to transformations outside the scope of the present
   181	development.  Consequently, no consumer of the lemma --- in the source or here
   182	--- requires the attainment form.
   183	
   184	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   185	
   186	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} states the lemma in the source shape.
   187	Its proof records the value-preserving construction and the approximate form
   188	that the construction yields, and explicitly marks the remaining attainment
   189	step as unproved, citing this note; an accompanying remark summarizes the
   190	obstruction.  An earlier revision of the blueprint had instead weakened the
   191	source-labelled conclusion to the approximate form; following the project's
   192	proof-gap protocol, the source-labelled statement is restored and the missing
   193	step is tracked in the proof rather than absorbed into the statement. The
   194	source-shaped declaration \leanid{exists\_symmetric\_projective\_strategy} is
   195	now linked to the lemma; its proof remains the tracked attainment obligation.
   196	
   197	\section{Conclusion}
   198	
   199	The verdict is a proof-level gap in the cited lemma: the symmetrization
   200	argument proves the given-strategy and approximate forms, while the printed
   201	conclusion additionally asserts that the supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ is
   202	attained, which does not follow.  The gap is harmless for the results built on
   203	the lemma, since both uses in the source, and all planned uses in this
   204	project, proceed from a given strategy of value at least $1-\eps$ or from a
   205	strict lower bound on the value, for which the value-preserving construction
   206	suffices.  For stage~4 (formalization) the recommendation is: formalize the
   207	given-strategy symmetrization lemma as the workhorse statement; keep the
   208	source-labelled lemma in source shape with the attainment step an explicit,
   209	tracked proof obligation; and do not strengthen the source-labelled statement's
   210	hypotheses or weaken its conclusion silently.  If a later investigation
   211	settles the counterexample question for symmetric games, the statement should
   212	then be reclassified from an unproved step to a documented statement
   213	correction.

    61	  Unless specified otherwise, all strategies considered in this paper are tensor
    62	  product strategies, and we simply call them \emph{strategies}.
    63	  Similarly, we refer to $\val^*(\game)$ as the \emph{value} of the game

    68	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]
    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if
    71	  all the measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ are projective.
    72	\end{definition}
    73	
    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}
    88	
    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using
    90	  a compact notation: we write $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ and
    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.
    93	
    94	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetric-strat}
    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}
   100	
   101	\begin{proof}
   102	  By definition for any $\eps'>\eps$ there exists a strategy $\strategy'= (\ket{\psi'},A,B)$ such
   103	  that $\val^*(\game,\strategy')\geq 1-\eps'$.
   104	Using Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}) we can assume
   105	without loss of generality that $\ket{\psi'}\in\C_{\alice'}^d\otimes \C_{\bob'}^d$ for some integer $d$
   106	  and that for every $x$, $A^x$ and $B^x$ are projective measurements.
   107	Let
   108	  \[
   109	    \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \big( \ket{0}_\alice \ket{1}_\bob
   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   111	    \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{\alice'\bob'}\big) \in (\C_{\alice}^2 \otimes
   112	    \C_{\alice'}^d) \otimes (\C_\bob^2 \otimes \C_{\bob'}^d)\;,
   113	  \]
   114	  where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ is obtained from $\ket{\psi}$ by permuting the two
   115	  players' registers.
   116	  Observe that $\ket{\psi}$ is invariant under permutation of $\alice\alice'$
   117	  and $\bob\bob'$.
   118	
   119	  For any question $x\in \cal{X}$ define the measurement $M^x = \{M^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$
   120	  acting on the Hilbert space $\C^2 \otimes \C^d$ as follows:
   121	  \[
   122	  	M^x_a = \ketbra{0}{0} \otimes A^x_a + \ketbra{1}{1} \otimes B^x_a \;,
   123	  \]
   124		i.e.\ for $\ket{\varphi} \in \C^d$, $M^x_a(\ket{0}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{0}A^x_a\ket{\varphi}$ and $M^x_a(\ket{1}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{1}B^x_a\ket{\varphi}$.
   125	  When Alice receives question $x$, she measures $M^x$ on registers $\alice \alice'$, and when Bob receives 
   126	  question $y$, he measures $M^y$ on registers $\bob \bob'$.
   127	Using that by assumption the decision predicate $D$ for $\game$ is symmetric,
   128	  it is not hard to verify that $\val^*(\game,\strategy) =
   129	  \val^*(\game,\strategy')$.
   130	\end{proof}

   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:comm-strategy}
   134	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let
   135	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\game$ such that  $\mH_A = \mH_B$.
   136	  Let $S \subseteq \cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$ denote the support of the question
   137	  distribution $\mu$, i.e.\ the set of $(x,y)$ such that $\mu(x,y)>0$.
   138	  We say that $\strategy$ is a \emph{commuting strategy for $\game$} if for all
   139	  question pairs $(x, y) \in S$, we have $[A^x_a, B^y_b] = 0$ 
   140	  for all $a
   141	  \in \cal{A}, b \in \cal{B}$, where $[A, B] = AB - BA$ denotes the commutator.
   142	\end{definition}
   143	
   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.

    44	\section{Key theorem forms}
    45	
    46	Three statements must be kept apart.  Throughout, $\game$ denotes a symmetric
    47	two-player one-round game and $\eps \ge 0$ a real parameter; the notation is
    48	introduced in the next section.
    49	
    50	\begin{enumerate}
    51	  \item \textbf{Source form (attainment form).}  If
    52	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and projective
    53	  strategy $\strategy$ with $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps$.
    54	  \item \textbf{Approximate form (what the source proof establishes).}  If
    55	  $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$, then for every $\eps' > \eps$ there exists a
    56	  symmetric and projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    57	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps'$.
    58	  \item \textbf{Given-strategy form (value-preserving symmetrization).}  If
    59	  $\strategy'$ is any strategy for $\game$ with
    60	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$, then there exists a symmetric and
    61	  projective strategy $\strategy$ with
    62	  $\val^*(\game, \strategy) = \val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps$.
    63	\end{enumerate}
    64	
    65	The source proof consists exactly of a proof of the third form, applied to a
    66	strategy supplied by the definition of the supremum; this yields the second
    67	form.  The first form asserts strictly more than the second, and the passage
    68	from the second to the first is the gap discussed in this note.  Every use of
    69	the lemma, in the source and in this project, consumes only the second or the
    70	third form.
    71	
    72	\section{The source assertion}
    73	
    74	A two-player one-round game
    75	$\game = (\mathcal X, \mathcal A, \mu, D)$ in compact symmetric notation
    76	consists of a finite question alphabet $\mathcal X$, a finite answer alphabet
    77	$\mathcal A$, a symmetric question distribution $\mu$ on
    78	$\mathcal X \times \mathcal X$, and a decision predicate $D$ treating the two
    79	players symmetrically.  A tensor product strategy
    80	$\strategy = (\ket\psi, A, B)$ consists of a unit vector $\ket\psi$ in a
    81	tensor product $\mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ of \emph{finite-dimensional}
    82	Hilbert spaces together with POVMs $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ for the two
    83	players; its value $\val^*(\game, \strategy)$ is the acceptance probability,
    84	and the value of the game is the supremum
    85	\begin{equation*}
    86	  \val^*(\game) = \sup_{\strategy} \val^*(\game, \strategy)
    87	\end{equation*}
    88	over all tensor product strategies.  A strategy is projective if all its
    89	measurements are projective, and symmetric if the state is
    90	permutation-invariant on $\mathcal H \ot \mathcal H$ and both players use the
    91	same measurements.
    92	
    93	The symmetrization lemma of \cite[Section~5]{Ji2020MIPStar} asserts:%
    94	\footnote{The statement is at
    95	\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~94--99,
    96	and its proof at lines~101--132.  The blueprint statement restored to this form
    97	is \path{lem:symmetric-strat} in
    98	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}.}
    99	if $\game$ is a symmetric game with $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some
   100	$\eps \ge 0$, then
   101	\begin{equation*}
   102	  \exists\, \strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M) \text{ symmetric and projective}
   103	  \quad\text{with}\quad
   104	  \val^*(\game, \strategy) \ge 1-\eps.
   105	  \tag{\path{lem:symmetric-strat}}
   106	\end{equation*}
   107	
   108	Its proof runs as follows.  For every $\eps' > \eps$ the definition of the
   109	supremum supplies a strategy $\strategy' = (\ket{\psi'}, A, B)$ with
   110	$\val^*(\game, \strategy') \ge 1-\eps'$.  By Naimark dilation in the completed
   111	projective form of \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} one may take
   112	$\ket{\psi'} \in \C^d_{A'} \ot \C^d_{B'}$ for some integer $d$ with all
   113	measurements projective.  One then forms the permutation-invariant state
   114	\begin{equation*}
   115	  \ket{\psi} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}
   116	  \bigl( \ket{0}_A \ket{1}_B \ket{\psi'}_{A'B'}
   117	       + \ket{1}_A \ket{0}_B \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{A'B'} \bigr)
   118	\end{equation*}
   119	on $(\C^2 \ot \C^d) \ot (\C^2 \ot \C^d)$, where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ permutes
   120	the two players' registers, and the block-diagonal projective measurements
   121	$M^x_a = \ket{0}\!\bra{0} \ot A^x_a + \ket{1}\!\bra{1} \ot B^x_a$.  Symmetry
   122	of $D$ gives $\val^*(\game, (\ket\psi, M)) = \val^*(\game, \strategy')$.  The
   123	construction is therefore \emph{value-preserving}: applied to any strategy it
   124	produces a symmetric projective strategy of exactly the same value.  What the
   125	proof establishes is thus the given-strategy form, hence the approximate form;
   126	the printed conclusion is the attainment form.
   127	
   128	\section{Why attainment does not follow}
   129	
   130	The supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ ranges over strategies on
   131	finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces of unbounded dimension.  The strategies
   132	$\strategy'_{\eps'}$ produced for $\eps' \downarrow \eps$ may require
   133	dimensions $d(\eps')$ growing without bound, and there is no compactness
   134	across dimensions from which a limiting finite-dimensional strategy of value
   135	at least $1-\eps$ could be extracted.  A symmetric projective strategy of
   136	value at least $1-\eps = \val^*(\game)$ would attain the supremum, so the
   137	printed conclusion is equivalent, under its hypothesis, to the assertion that
   138	$\val^*(\game)$ is attained by some strategy.  No general principle supplies
   139	this: it is known, and recalled in the introduction of the source itself, that
   140	the set of finite-dimensional quantum correlations is not closed and differs
   141	from the set of infinite-dimensional spatial correlations, so limits of
   142	finite-dimensional strategies need not be realized by any finite-dimensional
   143	strategy.  Whether some symmetric game realizes the failure --- a game whose
   144	value is attained by no tensor product strategy, presented together with the
   145	exposing functional as a decision predicate --- is a separate question that
   146	this note does not need to settle.  The local verdict is about the proof: the
   147	cited argument proves the approximate form and does not prove the attainment
   148	form.
   149	
   150	\section{Uses of the lemma}
   151	
   152	The source invokes the lemma twice.
   153	
   154	First, in the soundness proof for the oracularization transformation, the
   155	argument fixes a strategy $\strategy^{\mathrm{orac}}$ for the oracularized game
   156	``with value $1-\eps$'' and applies the lemma to assume without loss of
   157	generality that it is projective.%
   158	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/10_oracularization.tex},
   159	lines~317--321.}
   160	Here the input is a given strategy, not the value of the game; the
   161	given-strategy form applies verbatim and preserves the value exactly, so the
   162	use is justified by what the proof establishes.
   163	
   164	Second, in the soundness proof for answer reduction, the argument assumes the
   165	strict inequality $\val^*(\game) > 1-\eps$ and concludes that there is a
   166	symmetric projective strategy of value greater than $1-\eps$.%
   167	\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/11_answer_reduction.tex},
   168	lines~2322--2332.}
   169	Writing $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps_0$ with $\eps_0 < \eps$ and applying the
   170	approximate form with $\eps' = (\eps+\eps_0)/2$ produces a symmetric
   171	projective strategy of value at least $1-\eps' > 1-\eps$.  A strict lower
   172	bound on the supremum thus passes through the approximate form; attainment is
   173	not used.
   174	
   175	In this project, the soundness statements of the Pauli basis test track
   176	quantify over strategies assumed to succeed with probability at least
   177	$1-\eps$, so any symmetrization step starts from a given strategy and consumes
   178	the given-strategy form.  The blueprint currently records the lemma as part of
   179	the games vocabulary and has no downstream dependency on it; the two source
   180	uses above belong to transformations outside the scope of the present
   181	development.  Consequently, no consumer of the lemma --- in the source or here
   182	--- requires the attainment form.
   183	
   184	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   185	
   186	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} states the lemma in the source shape.
   187	Its proof records the value-preserving construction and the approximate form
   188	that the construction yields, and explicitly marks the remaining attainment
   189	step as unproved, citing this note; an accompanying remark summarizes the
   190	obstruction.  An earlier revision of the blueprint had instead weakened the
   191	source-labelled conclusion to the approximate form; following the project's
   192	proof-gap protocol, the source-labelled statement is restored and the missing
   193	step is tracked in the proof rather than absorbed into the statement. The
   194	source-shaped declaration \leanid{exists\_symmetric\_projective\_strategy} is
   195	now linked to the lemma; its proof remains the tracked attainment obligation.
   196	
   197	\section{Conclusion}
   198	
   199	The verdict is a proof-level gap in the cited lemma: the symmetrization
   200	argument proves the given-strategy and approximate forms, while the printed
   201	conclusion additionally asserts that the supremum defining $\val^*(\game)$ is
   202	attained, which does not follow.  The gap is harmless for the results built on
   203	the lemma, since both uses in the source, and all planned uses in this
   204	project, proceed from a given strategy of value at least $1-\eps$ or from a
   205	strict lower bound on the value, for which the value-preserving construction
   206	suffices.  For stage~4 (formalization) the recommendation is: formalize the
   207	given-strategy symmetrization lemma as the workhorse statement; keep the
   208	source-labelled lemma in source shape with the attainment step an explicit,
   209	tracked proof obligation; and do not strengthen the source-labelled statement's
   210	hypotheses or weaken its conclusion silently.  If a later investigation
   211	settles the counterexample question for symmetric games, the statement should
   212	then be reclassified from an unproved step to a documented statement
   213	correction.

   786	  have ha := measurement_outcome_nonempty (S₀.A hq.some.1)

   794	      _ = S₀.value := projectiveDilation_value S₀ a₀ a₀

    20	/-- Direct-sum carrier for the future heterogeneous role symmetrization.
    21	
    22	For a two-space strategy with Alice carrier `ιA` and Bob carrier `ιB`, the later
    23	symmetrized local space will use this tagged direct sum so that Alice's operators
    24	occupy the `Sum.inl` block and Bob's operators occupy the `Sum.inr` block. -/
    25	abbrev LocalCarrierSum (ιA ιB : Type*) := Sum ιA ιB
    26	
    27	/-- Local carrier planned for the heterogeneous symmetrization bridge: a role bit
    28	and a direct-sum carrier. This is the direct-sum analogue of the current
    29	same-space target `Role × ι` in `StrategyRole.lean`. -/
    30	abbrev RoleRegisterLocal (ιA ιB : Type*) := Role × LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB
    31	
    32	/-- Reassociate role bits and direct-sum carriers.
    33	
    34	This is the public heterogeneous analogue of the same-space role-register
    35	reassociation used internally by `StrategyRole.lean`. It prepares the target
    36	shape for reindexing block states on
    37	`(Role × (ιA ⊕ ιB)) × (Role × (ιA ⊕ ιB))`. -/
    38	def roleRegisterPairLocalEquiv (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    39	    ((Role × Role) × (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB × LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)) ≃
    40	      (RoleRegisterLocal ιA ιB × RoleRegisterLocal ιA ιB) where
    41	  toFun x := ((x.1.1, x.2.1), (x.1.2, x.2.2))
    42	  invFun x := ((x.1.1, x.2.1), (x.1.2, x.2.2))
    43	  left_inv := fun ⟨⟨_, _⟩, ⟨_, _⟩⟩ => rfl
    44	  right_inv := fun ⟨⟨_, _⟩, ⟨_, _⟩⟩ => rfl

    47	
    48	/-- Embed an operator on Alice's and Bob's original tensor product into the
    49	`(Sum.inl _) × (Sum.inr _)` block of the direct-sum tensor product. -/
    50	noncomputable def localPairABBlock {ιA ιB : Type*}
    51	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) :
    52	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB × LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) :=
    53	  Matrix.of fun x y =>
    54	    match x, y with
    55	    | (Sum.inl i, Sum.inr j), (Sum.inl i', Sum.inr j') => X (i, j) (i', j')
    56	    | _, _ => 0
    57	
    58	/-- Embed an operator on Bob's and Alice's original tensor product into the
    59	`(Sum.inr _) × (Sum.inl _)` block of the direct-sum tensor product. -/
    60	noncomputable def localPairBABlock {ιA ιB : Type*}
    61	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιB × ιA)) :
    62	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB × LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) :=
    63	  Matrix.of fun x y =>
    64	    match x, y with
    65	    | (Sum.inr i, Sum.inl j), (Sum.inr i', Sum.inl j') => X (i, j) (i', j')
    66	    | _, _ => 0
    67	
    68	@[simp] theorem localPairABBlock_AB_AB {ιA ιB : Type*}
    69	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) (i i' : ιA) (j j' : ιB) :
    70	    localPairABBlock X (Sum.inl i, Sum.inr j) (Sum.inl i', Sum.inr j') =
    71	      X (i, j) (i', j') :=
    72	  rfl
    73	
    74	@[simp] theorem localPairBABlock_BA_BA {ιA ιB : Type*}
    75	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιB × ιA)) (i i' : ιB) (j j' : ιA) :
    76	    localPairBABlock X (Sum.inr i, Sum.inl j) (Sum.inr i', Sum.inl j') =
    77	      X (i, j) (i', j') :=
    78	  rfl
    79	
    80	@[simp] theorem localPairABBlock_conjTranspose {ιA ιB : Type*}
    81	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) :
    82	    (localPairABBlock X)ᴴ = localPairABBlock Xᴴ := by
    83	  ext x y
    84	  rcases x with ⟨x₁, x₂⟩
    85	  rcases y with ⟨y₁, y₂⟩
    86	  cases x₁ <;> cases x₂ <;> cases y₁ <;> cases y₂ <;>
    87	    simp [localPairABBlock]

    90	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιB × ιA)) :
    91	    (localPairBABlock X)ᴴ = localPairBABlock Xᴴ := by
    92	  ext x y
    93	  rcases x with ⟨x₁, x₂⟩
    94	  rcases y with ⟨y₁, y₂⟩
    95	  cases x₁ <;> cases x₂ <;> cases y₁ <;> cases y₂ <;>
    96	    simp [localPairBABlock]

    98	@[simp] theorem localPairABBlock_mul {ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype ιA] [Fintype ιB]
    99	    (X Y : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) :
   100	    localPairABBlock X * localPairABBlock Y = localPairABBlock (X * Y) := by
   101	  ext x y
   102	  rcases x with ⟨x₁, x₂⟩
   103	  rcases y with ⟨y₁, y₂⟩
   104	  cases x₁ with
   105	  | inl i =>
   106	      cases x₂ with
   107	      | inl j =>
   108	          cases y₁ <;> cases y₂ <;> simp [localPairABBlock, Matrix.mul_apply]
   109	      | inr j =>
   110	          cases y₁ with
   111	          | inl i' =>
   112	              cases y₂ with
   113	              | inl j' => simp [localPairABBlock, Matrix.mul_apply]
   114	              | inr j' =>
   115	                  rw [Matrix.mul_apply, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   116	                  simp only [Fintype.sum_sum_type, localPairABBlock, Matrix.of_apply,
   117	                    zero_mul, Finset.sum_const_zero, zero_add, add_zero]
   118	                  exact (Fintype.sum_prod_type'
   119	                    (f := fun x : ιA => fun y : ιB =>
   120	                      X (i, j) (x, y) * Y (x, y) (i', j'))).symm
   121	          | inr i' =>
   122	              cases y₂ <;> simp [localPairABBlock, Matrix.mul_apply]
   123	  | inr i =>
   124	      cases x₂ <;> cases y₁ <;> cases y₂ <;> simp [localPairABBlock, Matrix.mul_apply]

   128	    localPairBABlock X * localPairBABlock Y = localPairBABlock (X * Y) := by
   129	  ext x y
   130	  rcases x with ⟨x₁, x₂⟩
   131	  rcases y with ⟨y₁, y₂⟩
   132	  cases x₁ with
   133	  | inl i =>
   134	      cases x₂ <;> cases y₁ <;> cases y₂ <;> simp [localPairBABlock, Matrix.mul_apply]
   135	  | inr i =>
   136	      cases x₂ with
   137	      | inl j =>
   138	          cases y₁ with
   139	          | inl i' =>
   140	              cases y₂ <;> simp [localPairBABlock, Matrix.mul_apply]
   141	          | inr i' =>
   142	              cases y₂ with
   143	              | inl j' =>
   144	                  rw [Matrix.mul_apply, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   145	                  simp only [Fintype.sum_sum_type, localPairBABlock, Matrix.of_apply,
   146	                    zero_mul, Finset.sum_const_zero, zero_add, add_zero]
   147	                  exact (Fintype.sum_prod_type'
   148	                    (f := fun x : ιB => fun y : ιA =>
   149	                      X (i, j) (x, y) * Y (x, y) (i', j'))).symm
   150	              | inr j' => simp [localPairBABlock, Matrix.mul_apply]
   151	      | inr j =>
   152	          cases y₁ <;> cases y₂ <;> simp [localPairBABlock, Matrix.mul_apply]

   154	theorem localPairABBlock_nonneg {ιA ιB : Type*} [Finite ιA] [Finite ιB]
   155	    {X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)} (hX : 0 ≤ X) :
   156	    0 ≤ localPairABBlock X := by
   157	  classical
   158	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite ιA
   159	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite ιB
   160	  rw [CStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_eq_star_mul_self] at hX ⊢
   161	  rcases hX with ⟨C, hC⟩
   162	  refine ⟨localPairABBlock C, ?_⟩
   163	  change localPairABBlock X = (localPairABBlock C)ᴴ * localPairABBlock C
   164	  rw [localPairABBlock_conjTranspose, localPairABBlock_mul]
   165	  exact congrArg localPairABBlock hC

   167	theorem localPairBABlock_nonneg {ιA ιB : Type*} [Finite ιA] [Finite ιB]
   168	    {X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιB × ιA)} (hX : 0 ≤ X) :
   169	    0 ≤ localPairBABlock X := by
   170	  classical
   171	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite ιA
   172	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite ιB
   173	  rw [CStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_eq_star_mul_self] at hX ⊢
   174	  rcases hX with ⟨C, hC⟩
   175	  refine ⟨localPairBABlock C, ?_⟩
   176	  change localPairBABlock X = (localPairBABlock C)ᴴ * localPairBABlock C
   177	  rw [localPairBABlock_conjTranspose, localPairBABlock_mul]
   178	  exact congrArg localPairBABlock hC

   180	/-- Swap an operator on `ιA × ιB` to one on `ιB × ιA`. -/
   181	noncomputable def heterogeneousSwapDensity {ιA ιB : Type*}
   182	    (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) :
   183	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιB × ιA) :=
   184	  Matrix.reindex (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) X
   185	
   186	/-- **Lean-only:** Tensor products commute with the heterogeneous swap map.
   187	
   188	Paper origin: `references/ldt-paper/inductive_step.tex:40-66`; this is the
   189	matrix-index identity used to identify the two role-register sectors in the
   190	heterogeneous symmetrization. -/
   191	@[simp] theorem heterogeneousSwapDensity_opTensor {ιA ιB : Type*}
   192	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   193	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA) (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιB) :
   194	    heterogeneousSwapDensity (opTensor A B) = opTensor B A := by
   195	  ext i j
   196	  rcases i with ⟨iB, iA⟩
   197	  rcases j with ⟨jB, jA⟩
   198	  simp [heterogeneousSwapDensity, opTensor]
   199	  ring

   201	theorem heterogeneousSwapDensity_nonneg {ιA ιB : Type*}
   202	    [Finite ιA] [Finite ιB] {X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)}

   204	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.reindex_nonneg (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) hX

   209	    heterogeneousSwapDensity (X * Y) =
   210	      heterogeneousSwapDensity X * heterogeneousSwapDensity Y := by
   211	  classical
   212	  unfold heterogeneousSwapDensity
   213	  exact map_mul (Matrix.reindexAlgEquiv ℂ ℂ (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB)) X Y

    26	/--

    37	  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]

    53	/--
    54	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    55	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation

    60	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    62	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    63	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=

    66	/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in

    70	noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    72	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    73	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
    74	  M.postprocess Prod.snd

    76	/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint

    79	def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]

    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in

    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB

   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B

   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ

   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-48`. -/
   124	noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re

   131	/-- Alice's marginal Born weight for an answer at a fixed question. -/

    18	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    24	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else
    28	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)

    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    33	def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    34	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
    38	  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ

    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    45	  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ

    51	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

+/-- The real quadratic form of an operator evaluated on a finite vector. -/
+private def vectorQForm {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ I) (A : Op I) : ℝ :=
+  (inner ℂ ψ (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A ψ)).re
+
+/-- Embed a bipartite state into the distinguished Naimark ancilla coordinates. -/
+private def padState
+    {I J α β : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) :
+    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((I × Option α) × (J × Option β)) :=
+  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((I × Option α) × (J × Option β)) ℂ).symm
+    (fun p => if p.1.2 = none ∧ p.2.2 = none then ψ.ofLp (p.1.1, p.2.1) else 0)
+
+/-- Padding a state by zero ancilla coordinates preserves its norm. -/
+private theorem padState_norm
+    {I J α β : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) :
+    ‖padState (α := α) (β := β) ψ‖ = ‖ψ‖ := by
+  apply (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mp
+  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
+  simp [padState, Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+
+/-- The padded-state quadratic form depends only on the distinguished
+compression of each local operator. -/
+private theorem stateQForm_padState
+    {I J α β : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
+    (A : Op I) (B : Op J)
+    (A' : Op (I × Option α)) (B' : Op (J × Option β))
+    (hA : ∀ i j, A' (i, none) (j, none) = A i j)
+    (hB : ∀ i j, B' (i, none) (j, none) = B i j) :
+    vectorQForm (padState (α := α) (β := β) ψ) (heteroKron A' B') =
+      vectorQForm ψ (heteroKron A B) := by
+  unfold vectorQForm
+  rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct, EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
+  change Complex.re (∑ p : (I × Option α) × (J × Option β),
+      (∑ q : (I × Option α) × (J × Option β),
+        heteroKron A' B' p q *
+          (padState (α := α) (β := β) ψ).ofLp q) *
+        star (padState (α := α) (β := β) ψ).ofLp p) =
+    Complex.re (∑ p : I × J,
+      (∑ q : I × J, heteroKron A B p q * ψ.ofLp q) * star ψ.ofLp p)
+  simp [padState, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, Fintype.sum_prod_type, hA, hB]
+
+/-- Choose the one-measurement Naimark dilation data for a POVM. -/
+private def oneMeasData
+    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) : OneMeasNaimarkData α I :=
+  Classical.choose (oneMeasNaimark M.toSubmeasurement)
+
+/-- The source submeasurement of the chosen Naimark data is the original POVM. -/
+private theorem oneMeasData_source_effect
+    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) :
+    (oneMeasData M).source.effect = M.effect := by
+  exact congrArg MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement.effect
+    (Classical.choose_spec (oneMeasNaimark M.toSubmeasurement))
+
+/-- Complete the Naimark projectors at one outcome to obtain a projective POVM. -/
+private def dilatedMeasurement
+    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (a₀ : α) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) :
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (I × Option α) :=
+  let P := completeAtOutcomeProj (oneMeasData M).toProjSubMeas a₀
+  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne P.outcome P.outcome_pos <| by
+    rw [P.sum_eq_total, P.total_eq_one]
+
+/-- Every effect of the completed Naimark measurement is a projection. -/
+private theorem dilatedMeasurement_isProjective
+    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (a₀ : α) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) :
+    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (dilatedMeasurement a₀ M) := by
+  intro a
+  let P := completeAtOutcomeProj (oneMeasData M).toProjSubMeas a₀
+  change IsProj (P.outcome a)
+  exact
+    { isIdempotentElem := P.proj a
+      isSelfAdjoint :=
+        (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (P.outcome_pos a)).isHermitian.eq }
+
+/-- Compressing a completed Naimark effect to the distinguished ancilla
+coordinate recovers the original POVM effect. -/
+private theorem dilatedMeasurement_compression
+    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (a₀ a : α) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) (i j : I) :
+    (dilatedMeasurement a₀ M).effect a (i, none) (j, none) = M.effect a i j := by
+  let D := oneMeasData M
+  let P := D.toProjSubMeas
+  have hcompress (b : α) : P.outcome b (i, none) (j, none) = M.effect b i j := by
+    change D.liftedEffect (some b) (i, none) (j, none) = M.effect b i j
+    rw [D.compression_none_none]
+    exact congrArg (fun X : Op I => X i j)
+      (congrFun (oneMeasData_source_effect M) b)
+  have htotal : P.total (i, none) (j, none) = (1 : Op I) i j := by
+    rw [← P.sum_eq_total]
+    simp_rw [Matrix.sum_apply, hcompress]
+    simpa [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrArg (fun X : Op I => X i j) M.sum_eq_one
+  simp only [dilatedMeasurement, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne]
+  change ((completeAtOutcomeProj P a₀).toMeasurement).outcome a
+      (i, none) (j, none) = M.effect a i j
+  rw [completeAtOutcomeProj_toMeasurement]
+  simp only [completeAtOutcome]
+  by_cases ha : a = a₀
+  · subst a
+    rw [dif_pos rfl]
+    rw [Matrix.add_apply, hcompress, Matrix.sub_apply, Matrix.one_apply, htotal]
+    by_cases hij : i = j <;> simp [hij, Matrix.one_apply]
+  · rw [dif_neg ha]
+    exact hcompress a
+
+/-- A unit vector has a nonempty coordinate type. -/
+private theorem nonempty_of_unit_vector
+    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ I) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) : Nonempty I := by
+  classical
+  by_contra hI
+  haveI : IsEmpty I := not_nonempty_iff.mp hI
+  have hzero : ψ = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
+  rw [hzero, norm_zero] at hψ
+  norm_num at hψ
+
+/-- A POVM on a nonzero finite-dimensional space has an outcome. -/
+private theorem measurement_outcome_nonempty
+    {α I : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Nonempty I]
+    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I) : Nonempty α := by
+  classical
+  by_contra hα
+  haveI : IsEmpty α := not_nonempty_iff.mp hα
+  let i : I := Classical.choice inferInstance
+  have heq := congrArg (fun X : Op I => X i i) M.sum_eq_one
+  simp [Matrix.sum_apply] at heq
+
+/-- Dilate both local POVM families of a strategy and pad its state by the two
+distinguished ancilla coordinates. -/
+private def projectiveDilation {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (a₀ : G.AnswerA) (b₀ : G.AnswerB) : Strategy G where
+  ιA := S.ιA × Option G.AnswerA
+  ιB := S.ιB × Option G.AnswerB
+  ψ := padState S.ψ
+  ψ_norm := (padState_norm S.ψ).trans S.ψ_norm
+  A := fun x => dilatedMeasurement a₀ (S.A x)
+  B := fun y => dilatedMeasurement b₀ (S.B y)
+
+/-- The local measurements of the Naimark-dilated strategy are projective. -/
+private theorem projectiveDilation_isProjective {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (a₀ : G.AnswerA) (b₀ : G.AnswerB) :
+    (projectiveDilation S a₀ b₀).IsProjective := by
+  constructor
+  · intro x
+    exact dilatedMeasurement_isProjective a₀ (S.A x)
+  · intro y
+    exact dilatedMeasurement_isProjective b₀ (S.B y)
+
+/-- Naimark dilation and state padding preserve every game correlation and
+hence preserve the strategy value. -/
+private theorem projectiveDilation_value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (a₀ : G.AnswerA) (b₀ : G.AnswerB) :
+    (projectiveDilation S a₀ b₀).value = S.value := by
+  unfold Strategy.value
+  apply avgOver_congr
+  intro xy
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro a _
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro b _
+  by_cases hw : G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b
+  · simp only [hw, if_true]
+    exact stateQForm_padState (α := G.AnswerA) (β := G.AnswerB)
+      S.ψ ((S.A xy.1).effect a) ((S.B xy.2).effect b)
+      ((dilatedMeasurement a₀ (S.A xy.1)).effect a)
+      ((dilatedMeasurement b₀ (S.B xy.2)).effect b)
+      (dilatedMeasurement_compression a₀ a (S.A xy.1))
+      (dilatedMeasurement_compression b₀ b (S.B xy.2))
+  · simp [hw]
+
+/-- Form the block-diagonal direct sum of two POVMs with the same outcome type. -/
+private def blockMeasurement
+    {α I J : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I)
+    (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α J) :
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (Sum I J) :=
+  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
+    (fun a => MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock (A.effect a) (B.effect a))
+    (fun a => MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_nonneg (A.pos a) (B.pos a))
+    (by
+      calc
+        (∑ a : α, MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock
+            (A.effect a) (B.effect a)) =
+          MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock
+            (∑ a : α, A.effect a) (∑ a : α, B.effect a) := by
+              simpa using MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_finset_sum
+                Finset.univ A.effect B.effect
+        _ = 1 := by
+          rw [A.sum_eq_one, B.sum_eq_one,
+            MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_one])
+
+/-- A direct sum of projective POVMs is projective. -/
+private theorem blockMeasurement_isProjective
+    {α I J : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α I)
+    (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α J)
+    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
+    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B) :
+    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (blockMeasurement A B) := by
+  intro a
+  change IsProj (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock
+    (A.effect a) (B.effect a))
+  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
+  · change MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock (A.effect a) (B.effect a) *
+        MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock (A.effect a) (B.effect a) = _
+    rw [MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_mul,
+      (hA a).isIdempotentElem.eq, (hB a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
+  · change (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock
+        (A.effect a) (B.effect a))ᴴ = _
+    rw [MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_conjTranspose,
+      (hA a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
+      (hB a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
+
+/-- Put a bipartite vector in the two exchanged off-diagonal sectors of the
+local direct sum, with equal amplitudes. -/
+private def symmState
+    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) :
+    EuclideanSpace ℂ (Sum I J × Sum I J) :=
+  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Sum I J × Sum I J) ℂ).symm fun p =>
+    match p with
+    | (Sum.inl i, Sum.inr j) => (Real.sqrt 2 / 2 : ℂ) * ψ.ofLp (i, j)
+    | (Sum.inr j, Sum.inl i) => (Real.sqrt 2 / 2 : ℂ) * ψ.ofLp (i, j)

+/-- The direct-sum state is fixed by exchanging its two local tensor factors. -/
+private theorem symmState_swap
+    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]

+  apply (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Sum I J × Sum I J) ℂ).injective

+  rcases p with ⟨p, q⟩

+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro q _
+    ring

+  ring

+    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]

+    (A C : Op I) (B D : Op J) :
+    vectorQForm (symmState ψ)

+          (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock A B)
+          (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock C D)) =

+      (∑ q : Sum I J × Sum I J,

+          (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock A B)
+          (MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock C D) p q *

+    (1 / 2 : ℝ) *

+          (∑ q : I × J, heteroKron A D p q * ψ.ofLp q) * star ψ.ofLp p) +
+        Complex.re (∑ p : I × J,
+          (∑ q : I × J, heteroKron C B p q * ψ.ofLp q) * star ψ.ofLp p))

+  simp only [Pi.star_apply, symmState_apply]
+  simp only [heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
+  simp only [
+    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_inl_inl,
+    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_inl_inr,
+    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_inr_inl,
+    MIPStarRE.LDT.ProjStrat.localDirectSumBlock_inr_inr,
+    zero_mul, mul_zero, Finset.sum_const_zero, zero_add, add_zero]

+      (∑ i : I, ∑ j : J,
+        (∑ k : I, ∑ l : J, A i k * D j l * (c * ψ.ofLp (k, l))) *
+          star (c * ψ.ofLp (i, j))) =
+        c * star c *
+          ∑ i : I, ∑ j : J,
+            (∑ k : I, ∑ l : J, A i k * D j l * ψ.ofLp (k, l)) *
+              star (ψ.ofLp (i, j)) := by
+    simpa only [Fintype.sum_prod_type, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
+      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply] using
+      (sesquilinear_sum_smul c (heteroKron A D) ψ.ofLp ψ.ofLp)
+  have hsecond :
+      (∑ j : J, ∑ i : I,
+        (∑ l : J, ∑ k : I, B j l * C i k * (c * ψ.ofLp (k, l))) *
+          star (c * ψ.ofLp (i, j))) =
+        c * star c *
+          ∑ j : J, ∑ i : I,
+            (∑ l : J, ∑ k : I, B j l * C i k * ψ.ofLp (k, l)) *
+              star (ψ.ofLp (i, j)) := by
+    simpa only [Fintype.sum_prod_type, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
+      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply] using
+      (sesquilinear_sum_smul c (heteroKron B C)
+        (fun p : J × I => ψ.ofLp (p.2, p.1))
+        (fun p : J × I => ψ.ofLp (p.2, p.1)))

+      (∑ j : J, ∑ i : I,
+        (∑ l : J, ∑ k : I, B j l * C i k * ψ.ofLp (k, l)) *

+        ∑ i : I, ∑ j : J,

+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro i _
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro j _
+    congr 1
+    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro k _
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro l _
+    ring

+    simp [c]
+  rw [hstar]

+    norm_cast
+    rw [← pow_two, div_pow, Real.sq_sqrt (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)]
+    norm_num
+  change Complex.re ((c * c) * _ + (c * c) * _) = _
+  rw [show c * c = (1 / 2 : ℂ) by simpa [c] using hsqrt]
+  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
+  ring

+/-- A symmetric distribution gives the same average after exchanging the two
+coordinates, independently of redundant zero-weight support entries. -/
+private theorem avgOver_prod_swap_of_weight_symm
+    {X : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
+    (μ : Distribution (X × X))
+    (hμ : ∀ x y, μ.weight (x, y) = μ.weight (y, x))
+    (f : X × X → ℝ) :
+    avgOver μ (fun xy => f (xy.2, xy.1)) = avgOver μ f := by
+  unfold avgOver
+  calc
+    (∑ xy ∈ μ.support, μ.weight xy * f (xy.2, xy.1)) =
+        ∑ xy : X × X, μ.weight xy * f (xy.2, xy.1) := by
+          symm
+          exact Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support μ _ fun xy hxy => by
+            rw [μ.outsideSupport xy hxy, zero_mul]
+    _ = ∑ x : X, ∑ y : X, μ.weight (x, y) * f (y, x) := by
+          rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+    _ = ∑ y : X, ∑ x : X, μ.weight (x, y) * f (y, x) := Finset.sum_comm
+    _ = ∑ y : X, ∑ x : X, μ.weight (y, x) * f (y, x) := by
+          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro y _
+          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro x _
+          rw [hμ]
+    _ = ∑ xy : X × X, μ.weight xy * f xy := by
+          rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+    _ = ∑ xy ∈ μ.support, μ.weight xy * f xy :=
+      Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support μ _ fun xy hxy => by

+        ((∑ a : G.Answer, ∑ b : G.Answer,
+          if G.decide x y a b then
+            vectorQForm S.ψ

+          else 0) +

+        ((∑ a : G.Answer, ∑ b : G.Answer,

+            vectorQForm S.ψ

+          else 0)) := by

+            rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+            intro b _
+            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+            intro a _
+            rw [← G.decide_symm]

+/-- Symmetrization preserves the value of a strategy in a symmetric game. -/
+private theorem symmetrizedStrategy_value {G : SymmetricGame}
+    (S : Strategy G.toGame) :

+  rw [strategy_value_eq_avgOver_payoff, strategy_value_eq_avgOver_payoff]

   250	private theorem stateQForm_reindex

250	private theorem stateQForm_reindex
   251	    {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   252	    (e : I ≃ J) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ I) (M : Op I) :
   253	    stateQForm (reindexState e ψ) (reindexOp e.symm M) = stateQForm ψ M := by
   254	  have hstate (j : J) : (reindexState e ψ).ofLp j = ψ.ofLp (e.symm j) := by
   255	    rfl
   256	  have hstate_star (j : J) : star (reindexState e ψ).ofLp j =
   257	      star (ψ.ofLp (e.symm j)) := congrArg star (hstate j)
   258	  have hop (j k : J) : reindexOp e.symm M j k = M (e.symm j) (e.symm k) := by
   259	    rfl
   260	  unfold stateQForm applyOperatorToState
   261	  rw [EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct, EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct]
   262	  change (Complex.re (∑ j : J,
   263	      (∑ k : J, reindexOp e.symm M j k * (reindexState e ψ).ofLp k) *
   264	        star (reindexState e ψ).ofLp j)) =
   265	    Complex.re (∑ i : I, (∑ k : I, M i k * ψ.ofLp k) * star (ψ.ofLp i))
   266	  simp_rw [hop, hstate, hstate_star]
   267	  apply congrArg Complex.re
   268	  have hinner (j : J) :
   269	      (∑ k : J, M (e.symm j) (e.symm k) * ψ.ofLp (e.symm k)) =
   270	        ∑ k : I, M (e.symm j) k * ψ.ofLp k :=
   271	    e.symm.sum_comp (fun k : I => M (e.symm j) k * ψ.ofLp k)
   272	  calc
   273	    (∑ j : J, (∑ k : J, M (e.symm j) (e.symm k) * ψ.ofLp (e.symm k)) *
   274	        star (ψ.ofLp (e.symm j))) =
   275	      ∑ j : J, (∑ k : I, M (e.symm j) k * ψ.ofLp k) *
   276	        star (ψ.ofLp (e.symm j)) := by simp_rw [hinner]
   277	    _ = ∑ i : I, (∑ k : I, M i k * ψ.ofLp k) * star (ψ.ofLp i) :=
   278	      e.symm.sum_comp (fun i : I => (∑ k : I, M i k * ψ.ofLp k) * star (ψ.ofLp i))

   280	/-- The product POVM whose effects are Kronecker products of the two factor effects. -/
   281	private noncomputable def tensorMeasurement
   282	    {α β I J : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   283	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   284	    (A : Measurement α I) (B : Measurement β J) :
   285	    Measurement (α × β) (I × J) :=
   286	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   287	    (fun ab => heteroKron (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2))
   288	    (fun ab => MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg (A.pos ab.1) (B.pos ab.2))
   289	    (by
   290	      change ∑ ab : α × β, opTensor (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) = 1
   291	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   292	      calc
   293	        (∑ a : α, ∑ b : β, opTensor (A.effect a) (B.effect b)) =
   294	            ∑ a : α, leftTensor (A.effect a) *
   295	              (∑ b : β, rightTensor (B.effect b)) := by
   296	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   297	          intro a _
   298	          rw [Matrix.mul_sum]
   299	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   300	          intro b _
   301	          exact (leftTensor_mul_rightTensor_eq_opTensor _ _).symm
   302	        _ = 1 := by
   303	          rw [rightTensor_finset_sum, B.sum_eq_one, rightTensor_one]
   304	          simp_rw [Matrix.mul_one]
   305	          rw [leftTensor_finset_sum, A.sum_eq_one, leftTensor_one])

   307	/-- The product of two projective POVMs is projective. -/
   308	private theorem tensorMeasurement_isProjective
   309	    {α β I J : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   310	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   311	    (A : Measurement α I) (B : Measurement β J)
   312	    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
   313	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B) :
   314	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (tensorMeasurement A B) := by
   315	  intro ab
   316	  change IsProj (Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2))
   317	  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
   318	  · calc
   319	      Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) *
   320	          Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) =
   321	        Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1 * A.effect ab.1)
   322	          (B.effect ab.2 * B.effect ab.2) := by
   323	            simpa using (Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul (A.effect ab.1) (A.effect ab.1)
   324	              (B.effect ab.2) (B.effect ab.2)).symm
   325	      _ = Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) := by
   326	        rw [(hA ab.1).isIdempotentElem.eq, (hB ab.2).isIdempotentElem.eq]
   327	  · exact (Matrix.IsHermitian.ext fun i j => by
   328	      rcases i with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
   329	      rcases j with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
   330	      simp [Matrix.kronecker, (hA ab.1).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.apply,

   341	    (by

docs/reports/issue-930-session48-orthonormalization-audit.md:76:### `thm:orthonormalization`
docs/reports/issue-930-session48-orthonormalization-audit.md:78:The paper states the orthonormalization theorem for a permutation-invariant state and a submeasurement `A = {A_a}` satisfying strong self-consistency:
docs/reports/issue-930-session48-orthonormalization-audit.md:91:The Lean theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.orthonormalization` has the same mathematical conclusion, expressed as an `SDDRel` between the left lifts of `A` and `P.toSubMeas` with error `orthonormalizationError zeta = 100 * zeta^(1/4)` (`Defs.lean:288-290`, `Orthonormalization.lean:674-688`). The permutation-invariance hypothesis is explicit as `PermInvState psi`, and the pure-state normalization convention is explicit as `psi.IsNormalized`; this is the formal counterpart of the paper's vector state convention and is already documented in #933.
docs/reports/issue-930-session48-orthonormalization-audit.md:101:The proof route matches the paper reduction from submeasurements to measurements. Lean completes `A` to `optionCompletion A`, whose `none` outcome is `I - sum_a A_a` (`Statements.lean:164-190`). The lemma `optionCompletion_bipartiteSSCRel` proves the completed measurement is strongly self-consistent with error `2*zeta` (`Orthonormalization.lean:58-173`), exactly reflecting the paper's `1 - 2 zeta` lower bound at `orthonormalization.tex:339-354`. The returned projective submeasurement on `Option Outcome` is restricted back to the original outcomes by `restrictSomeProjSubMeas`, and `qSDD_liftLeft_restrictSomeProjSubMeas_le` records that dropping the extra nonnegative summand cannot increase the distance (`Orthonormalization.lean:35-56` and `175-227`). This is the formal version of the paper's definition `P_a = \widehat P_a` for `a` in the original outcome set.

    91	    (hζ : 0 ≤ ζ) (hζ_le : ζ ≤ 1 / 4)
    92	    (hSpectral : SpectralTruncationStatement ψ A ζ)
    93	    (hsource :
    94	      ∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a - A.outcome a * A.outcome a) ≤ 2 * ζ) :
    95	    ∃ data : QLayerData Outcome ι,

    97	  projectiveLowRankSum_of_roundingWitness ψ A ζ hψ hζ hζ_le hSpectral.roundedFamily
    98	    hSpectral.toRoundingToProjectorsWitness hsource

   100	/-- **Rank reduction** (`\label{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}`).
   101	
   102	Paper origin: `references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:540-658`.

   104	The paper first applies `\label{lem:projective-non-measurement}` to obtain the
   105	rounded projective family `R_a`, and then performs the rank-reduction argument.
   106	This theorem keeps that source-facing boundary: the rounded family is produced
   107	internally from the source almost-projectivity estimate and is then passed to
   108	the internal constructor `projectiveLowRankSum_of_roundingWitness`. -/
   109	lemma projectiveLowRankSum {Outcome : Type uOutcome}
   110	    {ι : Type uι} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
   111	    [Fintype Outcome]
   112	    (ψ : QuantumState ι)
   113	    (A : Measurement Outcome ι) (ζ : Error)
   114	    (hψ : ψ.IsNormalized)
   115	    (hζ : 0 ≤ ζ) (hζ_le : ζ ≤ 1 / 4)
   116	    (source_almost_projective :
   117	      ∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a - A.outcome a * A.outcome a) ≤ 2 * ζ) :

   119	      RankReductionWitness ψ A ζ data := by
   120	  classical

   122	    projectiveNonMeasurement_of_sourceAlmostProjective_two_mul_full

   124	  exact projectiveLowRankSum_of_roundingWitness ψ A ζ hψ hζ hζ_le q hrounded
   125	    source_almost_projective

     5	
     6	Completeness estimates for the rank-reduced `Q` family in the paper's

     9	
    10	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

    16	noncomputable section
    17	
    18	/-- Under the small-error hypothesis `ζ ≤ 1/4`, the truncation error is at most `1/2`. -/
    19	lemma spectralTruncationError_le_half (ζ : Error)
    20	    (_hζ : 0 ≤ ζ) (hζq : ζ ≤ 1 / (4 : Error)) :
    21	    spectralTruncationError ζ ≤ 1 / (2 : Error) := by
    22	  -- Scalar bookkeeping for `ζ ≤ 1/4`: `√ζ ≤ 1/2`.
    23	  have hquarter : Real.sqrt (1 / (4 : Error)) = 1 / (2 : Error) := by norm_num
    24	  have hsqrt : Real.sqrt ζ ≤ 1 / (2 : Error) := by
    25	    exact hquarter ▸ Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hζq
    26	  simpa [spectralTruncationError, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow] using hsqrt
    27	
    28	/-- Under the small-error hypothesis `ζ ≤ 1/4`, the spectral truncation error
    29	is bounded by the fourth-root error scale used in the `Q/X/XHat/P` layer. -/
    30	lemma spectralTruncationError_le_zetaQuarterRoot (ζ : Error)
    31	    (hζ : 0 ≤ ζ) (hζq : ζ ≤ 1 / (4 : Error)) :
    32	    spectralTruncationError ζ ≤ zetaQuarterRoot ζ := by
    33	  have hζ1 : ζ ≤ 1 := by linarith
    34	  dsimp [spectralTruncationError, zetaQuarterRoot]
    35	  exact Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge' hζ hζ1 (by positivity)
    36	    (by norm_num : (1 : Error) / 2 ≥ 1 / 4)
    37	
    38	/-- **Completeness of `Q`** (`lem:Q-completeness`).
    39	
    40	If `Q_a` is the rank-reduced family from `lem:projective-low-rank-sum`, then
    41	its total operator `Q` has expectation at least `1 - 11 ζ^(1/4)`. -/
    42	lemma qCompleteness {Outcome : Type*}
    43	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    [Fintype Outcome]
    45	    (ψ : QuantumState ι)
    46	    (A : Measurement Outcome ι) (ζ : Error)
    47	    (data : QLayerData Outcome ι)
    48	    (hψ : ψ.IsNormalized)
    49	    (hζ : 0 ≤ ζ)
    50	    (hζ_small : ζ ≤ 1 / (4 : Error)) :
    51	    RankReductionWitness ψ A ζ data →
    52	      ev ψ (QTotal data) ≥ 1 - 11 * zetaQuarterRoot ζ := by
    53	  intro hRank
    54	  let diagA : Error := ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (A.outcome a * A.outcome a)
    55	  let qMass : Error := ev ψ (QTotal data)
    56	  let overlap : Error := ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (A.outcome a * Qa data a)
    57	  have hsdd :
    58	      qSDDOp ψ (A.toSubMeas : OpFamily Outcome ι) data.q ≤
    59	        roundingToProjectiveError ζ := by
    60	    simpa [SDDOpRel, sddErrorOp, avgOver, uniformDistribution, constOpFamily, qSDDOp]
    61	      using hRank.closeness.squaredDistanceBound
    62	  have hdiagA_nonneg : 0 ≤ diagA := by
    63	    unfold diagA
    64	    exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => by
    65	      simpa [Measurement.outcome_hermitian] using ev_adjoint_self_nonneg ψ (A.outcome a)
    66	  have hdiagA_le_one : diagA ≤ 1 := by
    67	    simpa [diagA] using
    68	      MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.subMeas_diagMass_le_one ψ hψ A.toSubMeas
    69	  have hsqrt_diagA_le_one : Real.sqrt diagA ≤ 1 := by
    70	    simpa using Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hdiagA_le_one
    71	  have hdiagA_lb : 1 - 2 * ζ ≤ diagA := by
    72	    have hsource := hRank.source_almost_projective
    73	    have hsum :
    74	        ∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a - A.outcome a * A.outcome a) = 1 - diagA := by
    75	      calc
    76	        ∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a - A.outcome a * A.outcome a)
    77	            = ∑ a, (ev ψ (A.outcome a) - ev ψ (A.outcome a * A.outcome a)) := by
    78	                refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    79	                intro a _
    80	                exact ev_sub ψ (A.outcome a) (A.outcome a * A.outcome a)
    81	        _ = (∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a)) - ∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a * A.outcome a) := by
    82	              rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    83	        _ = 1 - diagA := by
    84	              rw [← ev_sum ψ A.outcome, A.sum_eq]
    85	              simp [diagA, ev_one_of_isNormalized ψ hψ]
    86	    linarith [hsource, hsum]
    87	  have hqtotal_nonneg : 0 ≤ QTotal data := by
    88	    rw [← hRank.sum_eq_total]
    89	    exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => hRank.outcome_nonneg a
    90	  have hq_nonneg : 0 ≤ qMass := by
    91	    exact ev_nonneg_of_psd ψ (QTotal data) hqtotal_nonneg
    92	  have hdiagQ_eq :
    93	      ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (Qa data a * Qa data a) = qMass := by
    94	    calc
    95	      ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (Qa data a * Qa data a)
    96	          = ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (Qa data a) := by
    97	              refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    98	              intro a _
    99	              rw [(hRank.projective a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
   100	      _ = ev ψ (QTotal data) := by
   101	            rw [← ev_sum ψ (Qa data), hRank.sum_eq_total]
   102	  have hoverlap_le : overlap ≤ Real.sqrt diagA * Real.sqrt qMass := by
   103	    have hoverlap_abs :
   104	        |overlap| ≤ Real.sqrt diagA * Real.sqrt qMass := by
   105	      calc
   106	        |overlap|
   107	            = |∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (A.outcome a * Qa data a)| := by
   108	                simp [overlap]
   109	        _ ≤ ∑ a : Outcome, |ev ψ (A.outcome a * Qa data a)| := by
   110	              exact Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
   111	        _ ≤ ∑ a : Outcome,
   112	              Real.sqrt (ev ψ (A.outcome a * A.outcome a)) *
   113	                Real.sqrt (ev ψ (Qa data a * Qa data a)) := by
   114	              refine Finset.sum_le_sum ?_
   115	              intro a _
   116	              simpa [Measurement.outcome_hermitian,
   117	                (hRank.projective a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq] using
   118	                ev_abs_mul_le_sqrt ψ (A.outcome a) (Qa data a)
   119	        _ ≤ Real.sqrt diagA *
   120	              Real.sqrt (∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (Qa data a * Qa data a)) := by
   121	              simpa [diagA] using
   122	                Real.sum_sqrt_mul_sqrt_le (s := Finset.univ)
   123	                  (f := fun a => ev ψ (A.outcome a * A.outcome a))
   124	                  (g := fun a => ev ψ (Qa data a * Qa data a))
   125	                  (fun a => by
   126	                    simpa [Measurement.outcome_hermitian] using
   127	                      ev_adjoint_self_nonneg ψ (A.outcome a))
   128	                  (fun a => by
   129	                    simpa [(hRank.projective a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq] using
   130	                      ev_adjoint_self_nonneg ψ (Qa data a))
   131	        _ = Real.sqrt diagA * Real.sqrt qMass := by rw [hdiagQ_eq]
   132	    exact (abs_le.mp hoverlap_abs).2
   133	  have h_expand :
   134	      qSDDOp ψ (A.toSubMeas : OpFamily Outcome ι) data.q =
   135	        diagA + qMass - 2 * overlap := by
   136	    unfold qSDDOp qSDDCore
   137	    calc
   138	      ∑ a, ev ψ ((A.outcome a - Qa data a)ᴴ * (A.outcome a - Qa data a))
   139	        = ∑ a, (ev ψ (A.outcome a * A.outcome a) +
   140	            ev ψ (Qa data a * Qa data a) -
   141	            2 * ev ψ (A.outcome a * Qa data a)) := by
   142	              refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   143	              intro a _
   144	              have hcomm :
   145	                  ev ψ (Qa data a * A.outcome a) =
   146	                    ev ψ (A.outcome a * Qa data a) := by
   147	                exact ev_mul_comm_of_psd ψ _ _ (hRank.outcome_nonneg a) (A.outcome_pos a)
   148	              calc
   149	                ev ψ ((A.outcome a - Qa data a)ᴴ * (A.outcome a - Qa data a))
   150	                    = ev ψ ((A.outcome a * A.outcome a -
   151	                        A.outcome a * Qa data a) -
   152	                        (Qa data a * A.outcome a -
   153	                          Qa data a * Qa data a)) := by
   154	                          congr 1
   155	                          simp [sub_mul, mul_sub, Measurement.outcome_hermitian,
   156	                            (hRank.projective a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
   157	                          abel
   158	                _ = ev ψ (A.outcome a * A.outcome a) -
   159	                      ev ψ (A.outcome a * Qa data a) -
   160	                      (ev ψ (Qa data a * A.outcome a) -
   161	                        ev ψ (Qa data a * Qa data a)) := by
   162	                        rw [ev_sub, ev_sub, ev_sub]
   163	                _ = ev ψ (A.outcome a * A.outcome a) +
   164	                      ev ψ (Qa data a * Qa data a) -
   165	                      2 * ev ψ (A.outcome a * Qa data a) := by
   166	                        rw [hcomm]
   167	                        ring
   168	      _ = (∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a * A.outcome a)) +
   169	            (∑ a, ev ψ (Qa data a * Qa data a)) -
   170	            2 * ∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a * Qa data a) := by
   171	              rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]
   172	      _ = diagA + qMass - 2 * overlap := by
   173	            simp [diagA, overlap, hdiagQ_eq]
   174	  have hsq_gap :
   175	      (Real.sqrt qMass - Real.sqrt diagA) ^ (2 : Nat) ≤
   176	        roundingToProjectiveError ζ := by
   177	    calc
   178	      (Real.sqrt qMass - Real.sqrt diagA) ^ (2 : Nat)
   179	          = qMass + diagA - 2 * (Real.sqrt diagA * Real.sqrt qMass) := by
   180	              nlinarith [Real.sq_sqrt hq_nonneg, Real.sq_sqrt hdiagA_nonneg]
   181	      _ ≤ qMass + diagA - 2 * overlap := by
   182	            nlinarith [hoverlap_le]
   183	      _ = qSDDOp ψ (A.toSubMeas : OpFamily Outcome ι) data.q := by
   184	            rw [h_expand]
   185	            ring
   186	      _ ≤ roundingToProjectiveError ζ := hsdd
   187	  have hround_nonneg : 0 ≤ roundingToProjectiveError ζ := by
   188	    dsimp [roundingToProjectiveError]
   189	    exact mul_nonneg (by norm_num) (spectralTruncationError_nonneg hζ)
   190	  have habs :
   191	      |Real.sqrt qMass - Real.sqrt diagA| ≤ Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) := by
   192	    refine abs_le_of_sq_le_sq' ?_ (Real.sqrt_nonneg _) |>.2
   193	    calc
   194	      |Real.sqrt qMass - Real.sqrt diagA| ^ 2
   195	          = (Real.sqrt qMass - Real.sqrt diagA) ^ (2 : Nat) := by
   196	              rw [sq_abs]
   197	      _ ≤ roundingToProjectiveError ζ := hsq_gap
   198	      _ = (Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ)) ^ (2 : Nat) := by
   199	            calc
   200	              roundingToProjectiveError ζ
   201	                  = Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) *
   202	                      Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) := by
   203	                        nlinarith [Real.sq_sqrt hround_nonneg]
   204	              _ = (Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ)) ^ (2 : Nat) := by
   205	                    simp [pow_two]
   206	  have hsqrt_q_lb :
   207	      Real.sqrt qMass ≥ Real.sqrt diagA - Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) := by
   208	    have hleft := (abs_le.mp habs).1
   209	    linarith
   210	  have hq_lb :
   211	      qMass ≥ diagA - 2 * Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) := by
   212	    let s : Error := Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ)
   213	    let x : Error := Real.sqrt qMass
   214	    let y : Error := Real.sqrt diagA
   215	    have hxy : x ≥ y - s := by
   216	      dsimp [x, y, s]
   217	      exact hsqrt_q_lb
   218	    by_cases hys : y ≤ s
   219	    · have htarget : diagA - 2 * Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) ≤ 0 := by
   220	        dsimp [y, s] at hys ⊢
   221	        nlinarith [Real.sq_sqrt hdiagA_nonneg,
   222	          Real.sqrt_nonneg diagA,
   223	          Real.sqrt_nonneg (roundingToProjectiveError ζ),
   224	          mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hsqrt_diagA_le_one)
   225	            (Real.sqrt_nonneg diagA)]
   226	      linarith
   227	    · have hs_le_y : s ≤ y := le_of_not_ge hys
   228	      have hy_sub_nonneg : 0 ≤ y - s := by linarith
   229	      have hx_sq_ge : x ^ (2 : Nat) ≥ (y - s) ^ (2 : Nat) := by
   230	        nlinarith
   231	      have hx_sq_ge' :
   232	          qMass ≥ diagA -
   233	            2 * Real.sqrt diagA * Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) +
   234	            roundingToProjectiveError ζ := by
   235	        dsimp [x, y, s] at hx_sq_ge
   236	        nlinarith [hx_sq_ge, Real.sq_sqrt hq_nonneg, Real.sq_sqrt hdiagA_nonneg,
   237	          Real.sq_sqrt hround_nonneg]
   238	      have hcross :
   239	          2 * Real.sqrt diagA * Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) ≤
   240	            2 * Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) := by
   241	        have hmul :
   242	            Real.sqrt diagA * Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) ≤
   243	              1 * Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) := by
   244	          exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hsqrt_diagA_le_one (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)
   245	        nlinarith
   246	      linarith [hx_sq_ge', hcross, hround_nonneg]
   247	  have hzeta_term :
   248	      2 * ζ ≤ 2 * zetaQuarterRoot ζ := by
   249	    gcongr
   250	    have hζ1 : ζ ≤ 1 := by linarith
   251	    dsimp [zetaQuarterRoot]
   252	    simpa [Real.rpow_one] using
   253	      (Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge' hζ hζ1 (by positivity)
   254	        (by norm_num : (1 : Error) ≥ 1 / 4))
   255	  have hround_term :
   256	      2 * Real.sqrt (roundingToProjectiveError ζ) ≤ 8 * zetaQuarterRoot ζ := by
   257	    have hsqrt_rpow :
   258	        Real.sqrt (ζ ^ (1 / (2 : Error))) = zetaQuarterRoot ζ := by
   259	      rw [Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, zetaQuarterRoot, ← Real.rpow_mul hζ]
   260	      congr 1
